title: Stochastic SLI targets and error-budget auction for multi-variant endpoints
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Current SLOs are deterministic single-threshold contracts per endpoint or model variant. This does not capture the probabilistic behavior of conversational workloads where tail latencies and quality trade-offs matter across variants. During regional load spikes we need a principled way to reallocate limited error budget across variants and tenants.

Goal: Define a stochastic SLI/SLO model for multi-variant endpoints (e.g., standard/fast/quantized variants) and implement an "error-budget auction" mechanism that lets variants bid for error-budget credits. The auction will drive automated, auditable reallocation decisions when global or regional error budget pressure is detected. The outcome must integrate with circuit breakers and priority load-shedding so that degradation remains predictable, observable, and reversible.

Why unique: Rather than simple fixed priority or static throttles, this proposal formalizes probability-weighted SLI targets (quantile-anchored) and a lightweight auction that encodes business priorities and quality deltas to make real-time trade-offs defensible and measurable.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Stochastic SLI spec doc approved by Reliability and PM: includes metric names, quantiles, weightings per variant, and translation to effective error budgets.
2) Prototype auction simulator that ingests synthetic request traces and demonstrates consistent, predictable allocation decisions under at least three failure/pressure scenarios.
3) Telemetry: new metrics emitted (see monitoring_signals) with dashboards in Console that show live auction state and per-variant budget balances.
4) Circuit breaker integration: when auction signals forced shedding, circuit breakers pick correct variant fallbacks and provide human-readable reason codes.
5) Runbook and rollout plan validated in canary region with no customer-impacting regressions.
tasks: Write stochastic SLI/SLO specification (quantiles, time windows, weight model)
Design auction protocol and bidding schema (error-credit price, budget replenishment rules)
Build auction simulator and run scenario tests against historical traces
Instrument serving runtime: emit per-variant quantile histograms and error-budget state metrics
Console: add auction state panel and per-variant budget ledger visualization
Implement integration with regional circuit breakers and load-shedding controller
Create runbook: how to interpret auction outcomes and manual override steps
Canary rollout in eu-west-1 for 72h, monitor burn rates and customer impact
monitoring_signals:
Metrics to add/consume: 
- rts.sli.variant.{variant}.latency_p50, latency_p90, latency_p95, latency_p99 (ms)
- rts.sli.variant.{variant}.quality_p50, quality_p90 (model-specific quality score)
- rts.sli.variant.{variant}.error_budget_balance (unitless credits)
- rts.auction.region.{region}.current_price (credits/sec)
- rts.auction.region.{region}.active_allocations (list in dashboard)
- rts.circuitbreaker.{region}.{route}.state_change (enum reason_code)
Note: histograms must include tenant and route tags for attribution.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Spec and simulator (2 weeks) -> Phase 2: Telemetry + Console panel behind feature flag (2 weeks) -> Phase 3: Auction controller in canary region with passive mode (auditing only) (1 week) -> Phase 4: Activate auction with soft fallback thresholds and 72h observation (1 week) -> Phase 5: Full regional enablement and post-mortem.
Manual kill-switch: feature-flag per region + global emergency switch.
integration_notes: Auction controller will subscribe to existing telemetry streams (kafka topic: rts-metrics-v2) and publish allocation decisions to control plane topic (rts-controls). Circuit breaker service must accept decision envelope with reason_code and suggested fallback variant. We will add a small schema change to control API: decision_id, region, timestamp, allocations[].
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Kapoor: Kickoff notes: met with PM (Elena) and Reliability (Sam). Agreed to prototype auction simulator using last-quarter traffic slices and to include tenant-weighted bids.

2025-02-20 Marco Li: Simulator initial commit complete. Early observation: under synthetic surge pattern auction successfully protects high-value variants but oscillates when replenishment window < 30s. Need damping heuristics.

2025-02-25 Sam O'Neill (Reliability): Reviewed spec. Requested addition of break-glass thresholds and explicit reason codes for Console visibility. Also asked to ensure pricing curve monotonicity for auditability.
2025-03-01 Design review (Leah Park): Console panel mockups look good. Requested clearer lineage between allocation decision and downstream control actions for debugging.

2025-03-04 Marco Li: Implemented metrics emission (histogram + aggregate) and added stub consumer for auction controller. Pushed branch rts/auction-proto. Opening PR for Console integration next week.
risk_assessment: Medium risk: introduces automated reallocation of capacity which if mispriced could cause unnecessary quality degradation. Mitigations: passive canary, short initial windows, conservative default budgets, manual override and audit logs.
review_notes: Requested: add end-to-end test that validates decision audit trail and idempotency. PM asked for a simpler naming for error-credit units. Reliability asked to cap per-tenant spend to prevent noisy-neighbor budget exhaustion.
